supply_chain_view.thesis: AI data center bottlenecks are migrating from accelerator availability alone into the full AI factory stack: HBM and LPDRAM allocation, NAND/enterprise SSD supply, CPO/NPO optical links, FOPLP/CoPoS advanced packaging, 300mm capacity, MLCC supply, rack power, and liquid cooling.
supply_chain_view.strict_score_implication: The supply-chain thesis remains strong, and the revised score allows selective best buys after corrections when fundamentals and AI bottleneck power outweigh volatility, concentration, and event risks.
bottleneck_migration: Chip-level scarcity remains important, but rack-level integration now governs deployment speed.
Memory allocation is a persistent constraint across HBM, server DRAM, LPDRAM, NAND/Flash, and enterprise storage.
Networking bottlenecks are moving from pluggable optics toward 1.6T+ links, AECs, retimers, optical DSPs, lasers, and CPO/NPO architectures.
Power and cooling are no longer secondary infrastructure; grid-to-chip and chip-to-chiller designs shape how quickly AI capacity can go live.
